status: exact finite center and momentum-color witnesses plus a planar-limit spectral noncommutation counterexample; no finite-N R4 mass-gap transport

reductionStatement.planarClaim: at N=infinity, normalized neutral-sector Wilson-loop expectation values are volume independent when center symmetry and translation symmetry are unbroken
loopEquationInputs: large-N factorization closes products of normalized Wilson loops up to O(1/N^2)
unbroken center symmetry makes center-charged open loops vanish
matching action normalization and corresponding neutral observables
selection of the same physical solution of the loop equations
reductionStatement.finiteNBoundary: the equivalence is not exact at fixed N; connected correlators and reduction errors are generically O(1/N^2)
reductionStatement.originalFailure: the original one-site Eguchi-Kawai center symmetry breaks at weak coupling in four dimensions
reductionStatement.repairs: double-trace center stabilization, adjoint matter, quenching, or a suitable coprime twist can preserve the symmetry under additional conditions

clockHolonomyWitness.meaning: an evenly spaced center-symmetric holonomy converts adjoint color differences into momentum fractions of size 2 pi/(N L)

twistedOneSiteWitness.NRule: N=L_hat^2 for the symmetric four-dimensional twist
twistedOneSiteWitness.twistEaterConstruction: Gamma_1=P tensor I, Gamma_2=Q tensor I, Gamma_3=I tensor P, Gamma_4=I tensor Q with P Q=omega Q P
twistedOneSiteWitness.meaning: N^2 matrix basis elements reproduce the number of momentum points of an L_hat^4 lattice, so the effective linear size is a sqrt(N) in four dimensions

continuumOrderWitness.necessaryScaling: continuum plus infinite effective volume requires a sqrt(N) -> infinity; N proportional to a^-2 only holds the physical box fixed, while a growing box requires faster growth

planarSpectralCounterexample.fixedTimeLimit: for every fixed t, the second term vanishes as N tends to infinity and the planar correlator has apparent gap one
planarSpectralCounterexample.largeTimeLimit: for every fixed finite N, the small-residue state eventually dominates and the actual gap is 1/N
planarSpectralCounterexample.noncommutation: lim_N lim_t effectiveMass=0 while lim_t lim_N effectiveMass=1
planarSpectralCounterexample.lesson: O(1/N^2) control of amplitudes at fixed separation is insufficient to transport a uniform lower bound on spectral support

loopEquationBoundary.closure: factorization replaces expectation values of loop products by products of expectation values at N=infinity
loopEquationBoundary.centerCondition: open reduced-model paths must have zero expectation unless their displacement closes modulo the effective lattice
loopEquationBoundary.whatMatches: under the symmetry conditions, reduced and unreduced planar Schwinger-Dyson equations for corresponding neutral Wilson loops match
whatDoesNotFollow: uniqueness of the physically relevant solution of the infinite loop hierarchy
reflection positivity and a reconstructed Hamiltonian for the reduced solution
uniform control of large-area or large-time limits from pointwise 1/N^2 factorization
a positive lower spectral bound at every fixed finite N
the Clay statement for every compact simple gauge group

routeAssessment.successfulUse: reduction can calculate or numerically estimate planar string tensions, glueball correlators and running couplings using far fewer spatial sites
routeAssessment.strongestPossibleTheorem: a center-stable reduced construction plus unique reflection-positive planar loop solution and a positive planar gap would establish an N=infinity neutral-sector result
routeAssessment.missingFiniteNBridge: one additionally needs spectral convergence uniform near zero energy, excluding states whose overlap is O(1/N^2) while their energy tends to zero
routeAssessment.orderOfLimits: N to infinity, Euclidean time to infinity, volume to infinity and cutoff removal cannot be interchanged without uniform estimates

spin23Boundary.useful: large-N reduction is a computational and conceptual engine for compact internal SU(N) sectors and their planar observables
spin23Boundary.notAGroupBridge: Spin(2,3) has fixed rank and is noncompact; it has no Eguchi-Kawai N parameter whose infinity reconstructs spacetime
spin23Boundary.permittedAdjacency: a large-N internal sector may couple to a separately constrained massless Spin(2,3) gravitational sector, but reduction does not supply the gravitational Hilbert space or gap selected auxiliary modes

decision: Center-stable large-N reduction reconstructs planar momentum and loop equations, but it neither establishes a uniform spectral gap nor transports an N=infinity result to any fixed finite-N R4 theory. The obstruction is an order-of-limits and spectral-support problem, not a shortage of reduced matrix size.
